text:
Ross Colton has been the finishing piece of Nashville's winning run. He scored in three straight games in early November (CBS Sports), including a goal against Colorado, the team that traded him, in his first trip back to Ball Arena, and he has 4 goals in his last ten games.

This is not luck running hot. He has 4.74 expected goals on his own shots this season, about what his 5 goals say, and his 1.13 expected goals per 60 is a real rate for a player on about 13 minutes a night. The Predators have had 52.8% of the five-on-five expected goals with him out there, 7.2 points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey had him driving play last season in Colorado (96th percentile among forwards), with the caveat that he had strong teammates there too.

What to watch is ice time: it is up a minute and a half over his last ten games. If that sticks, our season range (about 20 goals at the midpoint) starts to look like the floor of what Nashville wants from him.
headline: Ross Colton is scoring against everyone, old teams included
